summary: Detector (7) of the PostToolUse nudge: records each edited file per (session,agent) and, once a SECOND distinct file is edited, names the files git history says move with them. Three rules, all measured, none to re-derive: the list clears on every new user message; nothing fires below 2 distinct files (trivial one-file jobs); then it fires for any partner not already edited and not already named — those two exclusions are the whole quieting mechanism, no per-session cap is needed. Two things a future editor will get wrong: (a) the tmp sweep must match the exact key or `<sid>_<aid>`, NEVER a bare `<sid>` prefix, or it clears a different session whose id merely starts the same; (b) the cache-dir derivation is a hand-copy of getCacheDir/cacheKey because hooks cannot import dist/ — change one and tests/cochange-nudge.test.ts is the only thing that notices. Cursor is why EDIT_TOOLS carries `SearchReplace` and editedPath accepts `path` as well as `file_path`; that shape is verified against Cursor transcripts, NOT against a live Cursor hook payload, so it accepts every shape rather than betting on one.
